episodes.title_en: Why Does Tightening a String Raise Its Pitch?
episodes.title_zh: 琴弦拉緊，音調為什麼升高？
episodes.question: How does tension change the pitch of the same guitar string?
episodes.description_en: With vibrating length held fixed, increasing string tension increases its vibration frequency and raises pitch.
episodes.description_zh: 固定同一根琴弦的有效振動長度，提高張力會使振動頻率增加，音調也會升高。

sources.title: Strings, standing waves and harmonics
sources.locator: Tension and tuning discussion, extracted lines 90–98, especially line 91 and the frequency formula.
sources.evidence: Increasing tension raises frequency; the fundamental depends on length, tension and linear mass density.
sources.limits: Ideal flexible string model. Real tightening slightly stretches the string; use a modest tuning change.

sources.title: The rule of strings and pitch
sources.evidence: Tightening raises pitch; thickness and vibrating length also affect pitch. Nut and saddle support the sounding string length.
sources.limits: Instrument-maker educational source, independent of UNSW; not a claim that length or thickness never changes in real tuning.

sources.title: Wave Speed on a Stretched String
sources.locator: Restoring-force/tension-component derivation lines 35–55; speed relation 64–73; frequency/length 95–97.
sources.evidence: For the same curved profile and linear density, larger tension produces larger transverse acceleration; wave speed increases with the square root of tension.
sources.limits: Small slopes, flexible string, approximately constant tension and linear density. Shorter-period bridge is author synthesis, not independent review.

sources.title: Travelling waves, superposition, reflection and transmission
sources.locator: Tension components and transverse acceleration, lines 15–20; Linear media, line 40.
sources.evidence: Local tension components accelerate and reverse string sections; small displacement gives an approximately proportional restoring force.
sources.limits: Second UNSW page counts as the same institution; Rice supplies the independent institution.

claims.text: For the same string with essentially fixed vibrating length and linear density, greater tension produces a higher vibration frequency and pitch.
limits: Compare one open string, with no fretting or string replacement. Modest tuning approximates fixed linear density. Pluck amplitude is not the pitch control.

claims.text: For the same small displaced profile and segment mass, greater string tension supplies a larger transverse restoring force. The same fundamental mode accelerates back more rapidly and has a shorter period.
limits: Author synthesis of tension-component force law and ideal-string period relation, awaiting independent factual review.
Keep local slope/curvature and linear density fixed. In the fundamental, the resultant opposes displacement, not velocity at every instant.

invariants: One open string between fixed nut and saddle throughout. No fretting, thicker replacement string or changing visible active length.
Both comparison strings show the fundamental: one spatial half-wave and two fixed endpoint nodes. More temporal oscillations, not more spatial loops, represent higher fundamental frequency.
Use the same pluck displacement and viewing scale so loudness is not substituted for pitch.
When showing tension arrows, they point outward at opposite endpoints. String transverse motion is perpendicular to its resting length.
The moving waveform is explicitly slow motion and its cycles are not literal audio-rate motion.
Freeze the same displaced profile for the restoring-force comparison; do not draw a greater initial bend on the tighter string.
At midpoint equilibrium crossing, restoring resultant is zero while speed is nonzero; never stop the string at its straight position.
episodes.simplification: Ideal fundamental-mode string with fixed active length and approximately fixed mass per unit length. Real strings have harmonics and stiffness; no exact pitch ratio is promised.

diagram_scale.string: Horizontal active length x=160..920, baseline y=850; endpoint nodes fixed.
diagram_scale.animation: Use y(x,t)=A*sin(pi*(x-160)/760)*cos(phase(t)), A=55 px for both conditions; tighter-string phase advances faster while both retain one half-wave.
diagram_scale.comparison: Compare 2 versus 3 schematic cycles in an equal visual time window, labelled 'Slow motion'; these are visual rates, not claimed measured notes.
diagram_scale.restoring_inset: Enlarge a midpoint segment. At downward displacement, tangent tension forces point up-left/up-right; horizontal components cancel and the resultant points toward baseline. For a 3/2 visual frequency ratio at equal density, a quantitative tension ratio is 9/4, not 3/2. Prefer unnumbered qualitative force arrows.

episodes.title_en: Why Does Water Climb a Paper Towel?
episodes.title_zh: 水為什麼會沿著紙巾往上爬？
episodes.question: How can water rise through paper without a pump?
episodes.description_en: Water wets cellulose fibers and spreads through tiny connected spaces. Capillary action can lift it against gravity, within limits.
episodes.description_zh: 水會潤濕纖維素纖維，並沿著連通的小空隙移動。這種毛細作用能讓水對抗重力上升，但並非沒有極限。

sources.title: Send Water Walking
sources.locator: Explanation of adhesion, cohesion and cellulose spaces, extracted lines 28–30.
sources.evidence: Paper towel has cellulose fibers and narrow spaces; attraction between water and fibers and between water molecules enables capillary movement.
sources.limits: Use wettable cellulose-gap mechanism only. Do not repeat an absolute adhesion-versus-cohesion inequality or its 'power balance shifts' inter-cup drainage account.

sources.title: Properties of Liquids
sources.locator: Paper towel Figure 10.19 and capillarity discussion, extracted lines 74–89 and 114–116.
sources.evidence: Adhesion to a porous material and cohesion within water explain wicking; in a simple vertical capillary, gravity limits rise.
sources.limits: An actual paper network is not a single uniform circular tube; do not apply its tube-height formula numerically to a towel.

sources.publisher: US Geological Survey Water Science School
sources.title: Capillary Action and Water
sources.locator: Capillary Action introduction, lines 19–24: relative tube surface area, upward force at liquid edges, surface continuity, gravity and paper towel.
sources.evidence: Wetting gives upward force at liquid edges; cohesion/surface tension maintains liquid continuity. Narrow channels increase relative wall influence; gravity limits rise.
sources.visit_result: OPENED_TEXT; fresh successful official /special-topics/ redirect to canonical page
sources.limits: Canonical requests intermittently timed out, but fresh redirected official text succeeded for this revision. Do not repeat simplified tall-tree transport claims.

claims.text: Wetting raises water at channel edges; cohesion keeps the liquid connected, allowing capillary flow through wettable spaces between cellulose fibers.
limits: Use untreated absorbent paper towel. Waxed or hydrophobic paper may behave differently.

claims.text: Capillary action can raise water against gravity, but does not provide unlimited upward rise.
limits: The simple-channel inset illustrates gravity opposing rise; real paper has irregular connected pores, and finite strip length or evaporation may limit the observed wet front first.

claims.text: For matching wettable cylindrical channels at equal column height, a smaller radius increases capillary upward-force-to-weight ratio: contact-line pull scales with radius while weight scales with radius squared.
limits: Author synthesis of relative wall influence and ideal capillary relation; awaits independent factual review.
Same surface tension, contact angle, density, height and gravity. Not a universal pore-network height or rate law; narrower does not mean faster wicking.

invariants: The bottom of the paper stays in contact with reservoir water; the wet front remains connected to the water supply through wetted spaces.
Draw a fixed irregular fiber network with gaps between fibers. Water fills these spaces and wets surfaces; do not portray solid fibers as empty drinking straws.
Molecular inset uses equal-sized water symbols throughout; no water molecules grow and no new pores appear as a mechanism.
Show adhesion to fibers and cohesion between water symbols separately; avoid a literal rope-chain of molecules with rigid bonds.
Gravity still points downward. Do not animate an endlessly rising water column or a self-powered recirculating pump.
On-image words, including schematic and time-compression labels, are English only.

Narrow/wide inset compares equal column height and the same liquid/wetting/gravity, identified as a 3D circular-channel model. Upward force acts at meniscus contact line, not uniformly from every wall pixel.
Do not show greater absolute capillary force in the narrow channel: halving radius halves upward pull but quarters water weight at equal height, doubling the ratio. No faster-wicking assertion.
episodes.simplification: A qualitative connected-pore explanation. The ideal capillary inset illustrates the direction of forces, not an exact pore shape, measured rise height or drying model.

diagram_scale.paper: Paper strip x=420..650, y=540..1270 with bottom y=1270 immersed below a reservoir surface at y=1190.
diagram_scale.fiber_inset: Separate 520 by 400 px inset with 8 stationary curved cellulose-fiber strokes and visible connected gaps; 12 equal-radius water symbols used only as a local schematic.
diagram_scale.time: Wet front moves upward over compressed time; no claimed centimetres or seconds. A separate simplified channel shows gravity, not a paper-height prediction.
diagram_scale.channel_comparison: Separate ideal cylindrical channels: diameters 80 vs 40 px, equal liquid height 180 px. Static qualitative upward-force bars may be 80 vs 40 arbitrary units, weight bars 50 vs 12.5; hide numerical units. Label 'Same height | Same liquid | Same wetting | Simplified channels'. Do not claim this is a common equilibrium or use it to set diameter-dependent wicking rates.

cues.en: Dip paper into water. Why does the wet patch climb above the surface?
cues.zh: 把紙巾一端浸入水中，濕的部分為什麼會爬到水面上方？
cues.visual: Untreated absorbent towel strip stays dipped in reservoir; wet front rises.

shot_plan.action: Untreated absorbent towel strip stays dipped in reservoir; wet front rises.
shot_plan.controls: Not every paper is wettable; no hidden pump.

cues.en: Between paper's fibers are tiny connected spaces that water can wet.
cues.zh: 紙的纖維之間，有水能潤濕的細小連通空隙。
cues.visual: Magnify a fixed fiber network with connected inter-fiber gaps.

shot_plan.action: Magnify a fixed fiber network with connected inter-fiber gaps.
shot_plan.controls: Fibers are solid, not hollow drinking straws.

cues.en: At their walls, attraction draws water upward along the edges: adhesion.
cues.zh: 在空隙壁面，附著的吸引作用讓水沿著邊緣往上爬。
cues.visual: Separate wetting-channel inset: concave liquid edge rises along wettable wall.

shot_plan.action: Separate wetting-channel inset: concave liquid edge rises along wettable wall.
shot_plan.controls: Curved meniscus stays connected to liquid below; no flying droplets.

cues.en: Water also attracts water. This cohesion keeps the moving liquid connected.
cues.zh: 水也會吸引水；內聚力讓正在移動的液體保持連續。
cues.visual: Neighboring equal-size water symbols remain within a continuous liquid region.

shot_plan.action: Neighboring equal-size water symbols remain within a continuous liquid region.
shot_plan.controls: Attraction indicators are schematic; no rigid chain of chemical bonds.

cues.en: So the rising edges can pull more water along through each narrow space.
cues.zh: 因此，往上升的邊緣也能帶動更多水，沿著狹窄空隙移動。
cues.visual: A connected wet front advances with reservoir water supplying it from below.

shot_plan.action: A connected wet front advances with reservoir water supplying it from below.
shot_plan.controls: No detached liquid blobs or one-way molecular ratchet.

cues.en: At equal height, narrower channels have more upward pull relative to their water weight.
cues.zh: 比較相同高度的水柱時，通道越窄，向上拉力相對於水重就越大。
cues.visual: Separate two cylindrical wettable channel models at equal water height; compare capillary pull and weight.

cues.en: This is capillary action. Gravity still pulls downward, so the rise has limits.
cues.zh: 這就是毛細作用。重力仍然向下拉，所以上升有它的極限。
